subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Jupiter: King of Planets
description: A 60-second lesson on Jupiter: King of Planets.

hook.text: Jupiter is so massive that 1,300 Earths could fit inside it. It outweighs all other planets combined.

buildup.text: It's a gas giant with no solid surface. Deep inside, hydrogen compresses into liquid metal.

discovery.text: Jupiter's gravity captures asteroids and comets, shielding inner planets from bombardment.

twist.text: It has at least 95 known moons. Europa may hide a liquid ocean with more water than Earth.

climax.text: Juno spacecraft found massive cyclones at Jupiter's poles arranged in geometric patterns.

punchline.text: So massive it shields us. The solar system's guardian.

quiz.question: Why is Jupiter considered a 'shield' for the inner solar system?
options: Its gravity captures asteroids and comets before they reach Earth
It blocks solar radiation with its magnetic field
Its size physically blocks debris from passing through

details.summary: Jupiter is the solar system's largest planet — so massive (318 Earths) that it contains more matter than all other planets combined. This gas giant has no solid surface, a powerful magnetic field, at least 95 moons, and a Great Red Spot storm larger than Earth that has raged for centuries.
details.whyItMatters: Jupiter shaped the solar system's architecture — its massive gravity directed comet and asteroid trajectories, possibly protecting Earth from frequent impacts.
takeaways: Jupiter is more massive than all other planets combined
It has at least 95 moons and a centuries-old giant storm
Its gravity shaped the orbits of everything in the solar system

faq.question: Could Jupiter have become a star?
faq.answer: No. Jupiter would need about 80 times more mass to ignite hydrogen fusion and become even the smallest red dwarf star. It does radiate more heat than it receives from the Sun (from gravitational contraction), but it's far too small for nuclear fusion. It's a failed star only in the loosest sense.

faq.question: What is inside Jupiter?
faq.answer: Beneath the visible cloud tops, hydrogen gas gradually compresses into liquid, then into a bizarre state called metallic hydrogen — where extreme pressure forces hydrogen to conduct electricity. This metallic hydrogen generates Jupiter's enormous magnetic field.
